*   Goal: Parallelize an N-body gravitational acceleration kernel using OpenMP.
    *   Constraint: Change only code between `=== KERNEL BEGIN ===` and `=== KERNEL END ===`.
    *   Compiler: `clang -O2 -fopenmp` (OpenMP 5.1).

    *   Core operation: $\sum_{j} \frac{m_j (\vec{p}_j - \vec{p}_i)}{(|\vec{p}_j - \vec{p}_i|^2 + \epsilon)^{3/2}}$.

    *   The `omp simd` pragma is used in the previous answer.

    ```c
    static void kernel(int n, const double *px, const double *py, const double *pz,
                       const double *m, double *ax, double *ay, double *az) {
        const double * restrict rpx = px;
        const double * restrict rpy = py;
        const double * restrict rpz = pz;
        const double * restrict rm = m;
        double * restrict rax = ax;
        double * restrict ray = ay;
        double * restrict raz = az;

        #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            double pix = rpx[i];
            double piy = rpy[i];
            double piz = rpz[i];
            double sx = 0.0, sy = 0.0, sz = 0.0;

            #pragma omp simd reduction(+:sx, sy, sz)
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                double dx = rpx[j] - pix;
                double dy = rpy[j] - piy;
                double dz = rpz[j] - piz;
                double r2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + 1e-9;
                double inv = rm[j] / (r2 * sqrt(r2));
                sx += dx * inv;
                sy += dy * inv;
                sz += dz * inv;
            }
            rax[i] = sx;
            ray[i] = sy;
            raz[i] = sz;
        }
    }
    ```

    ```c
                const double dz = rpz[j] - piz;
                const double r2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + 1e-9;
                const double inv_r = 1.0 / sqrt(r2);
                const double inv = rm[j] * inv_r * inv_r * inv_r;
                sx += dx * inv;
                sy += dy * inv;
                sz += dz * inv;
            }
            rax[i] = sx;
            ray[i] = sy;
            raz[i] = sz;
        }
    }
    ```
    Wait, is `inv_r * inv_r * inv_r` really faster than `r2 * sqrt(r2)`?
    `r2 * sqrt(r2)`: 1 `sqrt`, 1 `mul`, 1 `div`.
    `inv_r * inv_r * inv_r`: 1 `sqrt`, 1 `div`, 3 `mul`.
    If `1.0 / sqrt(r2)` is fast, then the second one is better.
    But `1.0 / (r2 * sqrt(r2))` also has a `1.0 /` (division).
    So the number of divisions is the same.
    The difference is whether `1.0 / sqrt(r2)` can be optimized as a single `rsqrt` instruction.
    In Clang, `1.0 / sqrt(x)` is a very strong candidate for this.
